title: College Enrollment
scope: This ledger ranks states on IPEDS Fall 2024 enrollment in degree-granting postsecondary institutions, and also reports 2023 SAT mean scores by state, public FTE faculty and staff and students-per-faculty for Fall 2023 (Digest 314.50), IPEDS 6-year bachelor's graduation rates by state for the 2017 cohort, bachelor's degrees conferred in 2023-24, degree-granting institution counts for 2022-23, public 4-year in-state tuition and fees for 2022-23, SHEF FY 2025 education appropriations and state-and-local support, and Digest public higher-education expenditures for 2020-21. National full-time faculty composition (rank and sex) remains on Digest 315.20.
exclusions: Does not cover K-12, rankings of individual colleges as advice, or predictions of admission. ACT state means are not in the current Digest xlsx set.
heritage: Formerly Higher Education College Admissions, Enrollment, Faculty and Staff, and Student Data
vintage_note: Rebuilt Aug 19, 2026 from IPEDS 2024-25 provisional DRVEF2024 ENRTOT joined to HD2024 on UNITID for degree-granting institutions (DEGGRANT=1). Digest table 304.10 still ends at Fall 2022; that history stays on the trend and 2024 is the IPEDS point. Later views compiled Aug 19, 2026 are stored under derived.secondary.

lead: Fall enrollment in degree-granting postsecondary institutions was 19,760,570 in 2024 (SRC-608-01). Massachusetts enrolled 482,004, rank 14 of 51 (derived, SRC-608-01). The SAT mean total score for 2023 graduates was 1028 in the United States, with 51.2% of graduates taking the test (SRC-608-02). Massachusetts scored 1112 (57.0% taking the test) (SRC-608-02). Degree-granting institutions employed 1,530,513 faculty in Fall 2023 (SRC-608-03). The IPEDS 6-year bachelor's graduation rate for the 2017 entry cohort was 64.5% nationally; Massachusetts was 75.0%, rank 2 of 51 (derived, SRC-608-12). Public institutions employed 11,022 FTE faculty in Massachusetts in Fall 2023, rank 24 of 51 (derived, SRC-608-06). Public 4-year in-state tuition and fees were $14,345 in Massachusetts in 2022-23 (SRC-608-09). SHEF education appropriations were $130.71 billion nationally in FY 2025; Massachusetts was $2.60 billion, rank 13 of 51 (derived, SRC-608-07). Degree-granting institutions conferred 1,959,325 bachelor's degrees in 2023-24; Massachusetts conferred 57,881, rank 10 of 51 (derived, SRC-608-10). Full-time faculty numbered 859,825 in Fall 2023; 192,300 were professors and 48.8% were women (SRC-608-05).

ipeds_6yr_grad_by_state_2017.note: IPEDS GR2023 joined to HD2023 on UNITID. The national rollup is 64.5 percent, matching Digest 326.10.
